name: Pedagogical Query Frequency
description: Measures the absolute frequency of interrogative sentences and question words (e.g., 'who', 'what', 'how', 'why') used to simulate a conversational or educational tone. High-parameter Language Models, fine-tuned on instruction-following datasets and tutorials, harbor a strong algorithmic bias toward assuming a 'didactic' (teacher-student) persona. They chronically overuse questions to artificially stimulate reader engagement or purely to set up the next block of generated information.
algorithm: Interrogative Lexicon and Query Ratio Analysis
mechanism: The algorithm counts interrogative pronouns, adverbs, and terminal question marks, calculating the ratio of query sentences to declarative sentences. During RLHF training, models are rewarded for being helpful, thorough, and engaging, which mathematically reinforces the 'Pedagogical Query Pattern'—where the AI asks a question ('How do we implement this?') entirely so it can immediately answer it. Human writers in professional contexts typically state facts or transition smoothly, whereas AI texts exhibit a high frequency of these self-contained 'Query-Answer' loops, elevating the interrogative frequency far beyond normal human baselines.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing explanatory articles, tutorials, and corporate communications where the AI's overly helpful, 'teacher-like' questioning tone feels artificial and condescending compared to mature human writing.
strengths:
• Excellent at exposing the default 'helpful assistant' persona embedded in almost all commercial LLMs.
• Very computationally efficient, relying on robust token counting and sentence classification.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives in genuine educational materials, study guides, or interactive Q&A articles where high question frequency is the required format.
• Easily bypassed if the user explicitly prompts the AI to 'write declaratively without asking any questions'.
parameters:
Analysis: Interrogative Token Extraction and Query/Declarative Ratio
Metric: Frequency of Questions per 100 Sentences
Output: 0-100 Pedagogical Query (Conversational Simulation) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 75-85% accuracy in essays and articles. It provides a strong signal of AI 'conversational padding' when paired with Sentence Length Variance.

references.title: Manning, C.D. & Schütze, H. (1999). Foundations of Statistical Natural Language Processing. MIT Press.
Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
